correctness.rationale: The proof asserts aff(F_G(a))=x0+ker B for an arbitrary feasible netflow; this can fail when some coordinate is identically zero on the nonnegative-flow fiber. Explicit counterexample: V={0,1,2,3}, E ordered (0→1),(0→2),(1→2),(0→3),(2→3), netflow a=(1,0,−1,0). The directed graph is acyclic, its underlying undirected graph is connected, a is integral and sums to zero, and F_G(a)={x(t)=(t,1−t,t,0,0):0≤t≤1}, a positive-dimensional segment of intrinsic length sqrt3. Its actual inradius equals sqrt3/2≈0.8660254038. All and only x01,x02,x12 are nontrivial coordinate facets. The full-graph Laplacian gives 1−R for these edges (3/8,1/2,3/8), respectively (and 3/8 on both forced-zero edges). Nontrivial lower ideals S={0} and S={0,1} have a(S)=1 and C(S)=sqrt(3/8)+sqrt(1/2); S={0,1,2} has C=0. Thus the claimed formula returns 1/[sqrt(3/8)+sqrt(1/2)]=4/(sqrt6+2sqrt2)≈0.7578747639, not sqrt3/2. Indeed the actual affine tangent is span(1,−1,1,0,0), strictly smaller than ker B, so full-graph cycle projections give incorrect facet-distance factors. Numerical evaluations only illustrate an exact inequality of radicals; rational Laplacian leverage and segment parameterization were calculated independently. Existing three bundled tests happen to have full-dimensional affine incidence fibers, so VERIFY_OK does not validate this missing hypothesis. Original universal claim is false and must be rejected, not passed with a disclaimer or a purely prospective fix.
residual_risks: Full-graph projection formula itself is correct on ker B; counterexample identifies its misuse, not a failure of electrical network theory.
A restricted theorem might hold after support reduction or a suitable relative-interior full support hypothesis, but no complete repaired package is supplied.
